title: The Exodar
body: The Exodar was never meant to be a city. It was a dimensional ship, a satellite of Tempest Keep, the fortress the naaru brought to the Netherstorm of Outland. When Prince Kael'thas and his blood elves seized the keep and captured the naaru M'uru, the naaru O'ros barred them from its own section and hid within the vessel. Prophet Velen led a raid to take it and flee in search of allies on Azeroth, but blood elf saboteurs crippled the ship, and it came down on the western side of Azuremyst Isle, crashing into the flank of a mountain. The draenei made its largest surviving section their capital. Its heart is the round Seat of the Naaru, where O'ros still dwells, and from it branch the Crystal Hall of the shaman, the Vault of Lights where Velen keeps his court, and the busy Trader's Tier. Elekks wait outside the entrance, and from a dock below the western wall ships sail to Auberdine, the nearest town of the Alliance the draenei have joined.

title: Seat of the Naaru
body: At the center of the Exodar lies the Seat of the Naaru, a great round hall with a shimmer of purple light at its heart. On its lowest level dwells the naaru O'ros. Around the rim open the bank and the auction house, and the city's peacekeepers greet visitors with the blessings of the naaru. Herald Bran'daan cries the latest news from both continents, from the Plaguelands to Feathermoon Stronghold. Off the spiral ramp of the main entrance, Caregiver Breel keeps the inn called the Exobar. Not all of the ship survived: two artificers stand before a district ruined in the crash, and from time to time the great hull still shudders.

title: The Crystal Hall
body: The Crystal Hall forms the northern wing of the Exodar, a quiet place built around a shining pool known as the Light Blessed Waters. It belongs to the shaman. Farseer Nobundo teaches here with Sulaa, Gurrag and Hobahken, who bid their pupils respect the elements of this world and the balance its spirits keep. Seer Skaltesh, guide to the shaman seeking enlightenment, offers even those on other paths a draught of elemental sapta, and with it they glimpse the many elemental spirits that share the hall unseen. Broken miners work a small cavern of crystal off to one side. Enchanters, jewelcrafters and scribes teach their trades nearby.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Crystal_Hall (northern wing, Light Blessed Waters, crystal-mining cavern, scrolls in naaru runes, trainers, Seer Skaltesh and Sapta Sight revealing many elementals)

title: The Vault of Lights
body: The Vault of Lights, the Exodar's western wing, is a house of the Light and of learning; a spiral walkway climbs from it to a second entrance above Valaar's Berth. Paladins train with Jol in the glowing Vindicators' Sanctum; priests gather in the Anchorites' Sanctum and mages in the Hall of the Mystics, where a portal opens onto the Blasted Lands. Holographic emitters run a museum of the Burning Legion, naming each servant of the enemy for passing tour groups, down to the eredar, once the draenei's own noble kinsmen. Prophet Velen keeps to the upper platform under the watch of his guards, the Shield of Velen, and there too volunteers are called to the battlefields of Azeroth and Northrend.

title: Trader's Tier
body: The Trader's Tier, the southern wing of the Exodar, holds most of the city's craftsmen and merchants. Smiths, engineers, leatherworkers and tailors keep their corners, and vendors sell weapons and armor of every weight. The ship's stores are thin. Dugiru, the cloth quartermaster, warns that the Exodar's once vast supply of textiles has dwindled dangerously low, and asks friends of the draenei for donations. Up the stairs lies the Hunters' Sanctum, where Ganaar passes on what he learned from the furbolgs about caring for beasts. At the top of a ramp, the highest point of the tier, warriors train on the Ring of Arms, where Behomat hands the little salvaged from the wreckage to those most able to use it.

title: Prophet Velen
body: Prophet Velen leads the draenei. On Argus he ruled the eredar beside Kil'jaeden and Archimonde, and when Sargeras offered them power, a vision showed Velen the price: worlds destroyed and his people turned to demons. He fled with those who would follow, and the Burning Legion has hunted the draenei ever since and found them even on Draenor, where the corrupted orcs slaughtered them. Now he holds court in the Vault of Lights. As his people seek this world's help against the Legion, he reminds them that they must also learn to live peaceably among its peoples. He welcomes the Broken as well, and calls the shamanism they teach critical to the draenei's future.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Velen (Triumvirate with Kil'jaeden and Archimonde, Sargeras' offer, vision from the naaru K'ure, flight from Argus, Draenor and the orc genocide, raid on the Exodar)

notes: Faction 1: template 1640 has the Horde as enemy group. 9461 (Tuluun to Velen) is used only as a trigger; Azuremyst's 352434 tells the Call of Fire chain. The Bloodmyst quests he gives or ends (9698, 9699, 9762) are left to Bloodmyst. The Light-infused artifact quest 12776 is from the removed 3.0.2 event and is not used. Elemental Unrest (4.0), Rakeesh and the Argus campaign left out. Fact-check: the wiki's attribution of the vision to K'ure is not clearly pre-Cataclysm, so the vision is left unattributed.

title: O'ros
body: O'ros is the naaru who came to Azeroth with the draenei and dwells deep in the Seat of the Naaru. With A'dal and M'uru it brought Tempest Keep to the Netherstorm. When Kael'thas Sunstrider's blood elves took the keep and captured M'uru, O'ros barred them from its own section and hid within the vessel that became the Exodar. The draenei hold it dear enough that one exarch swears by its beardless, geometric head. The blood elves have not forgotten it either: their agents on the isles mean to enslave O'ros, as they did M'uru, and take back the ship.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/O'ros (came with A'dal and M'uru, stayed with M'uru at Tempest Keep, barred the elves from its section, hid in the satellite that became the Exodar)

title: Farseer Nobundo
body: Farseer Nobundo was a vindicator of Draenor until the orcs' fel magic twisted him into one of the Broken and cut him off from the Light. He went on pilgrimage to learn why and waited decades by an oasis for an answer that never came. Then a wind rose that would not stop, and in its voice he learned the truth: the Light had not forsaken the Broken, and the elements offered another path. When he came home, Velen, who had foreseen it, asked him to lead the Broken and teach shamanism to all. Many still despise the Broken or call the shaman's way blasphemy; Nobundo asks his pupils not to judge the flame by its outward appearance, nor him.

title: Torallius and Aalun
body: Outside the Exodar's entrance, the elekk pens belong to Torallius the Pack Handler, a one-eyed breeder of the great beasts the draenei brought from Draenor. He trusts no outsider with his elekks until they prove their friendship to his people. When Exarch Menelaous sends him promising youngsters with orders for the front on Bloodmyst Isle, he asks whether this is the best the Hand of Argus can do and swears the newcomer will never make it, then sends them on anyway. Beside him the riding trainer Aalun offers to teach the riding of the finest beasts anyone has seen, for a price, but not to outsiders the draenei do not hold in the highest esteem.

title: Huntress Kella Nightbow
body: Huntress Kella Nightbow is a night elf who keeps watch near Valaar's Berth, west of the Exodar, and every young draenei hunter is sent to her to learn the taming of beasts. Her method comes from the Stillpine furbolgs, who carve totems in the likeness of an animal that let a hunter bond with such a creature for a time. Her pupils begin with the feisty barbed crawlers of the western coast, move on to the greater timberstriders of the north and finish with a nightstalker. She jokes that the timberstrider did not peck their eyes out, not that she thought it would. Then she sends them to Ganaar in the Trader's Tier.

title: The Draenei Call of Water
body: When a draenei shaman has grown in wisdom, Farseer Nobundo calls them back to the Crystal Hall to learn the mysteries of water. A powerful water elemental, Aqueous, has asked for help: something is throwing the waters of Bloodmyst Isle out of balance, and Nobundo is not surprised, given the blood elves' unnatural ways. With a potion to help them reach her, the shaman finds Aqueous in a hidden reef beneath the waves off the island's northern shore, where she speaks with them mind to mind. Essences drawn from her tainted sisters in the Foul Pool show the corruption is worse than feared, potent enough to ride the ocean currents across all of Azeroth. Its source is the camp of Tel'athion the Impure, whose demented research seeps filth into the island's water. Water of great purity, poured over his barrels, draws him out to his end. Aqueous keeps back a little of it, sure of the shaman's success, and Nobundo binds its essence into a powerful water totem.
sources: quests 9500, 9502, 10490 (Sulaa, Farseer Javad in Ironforge, Farseer Umbrua in Stormwind send the shaman to Nobundo)
quest 9501 description and reward text (Aqueous, imbalance on Bloodmyst, blood elves' unnatural predilections, potion, hidden reef off the northern shore, speaking with minds)
quests 9503, 9504 (Foul Pool essences of her unfortunate sisters, corruption could spread on ocean currents, pure water sample)
quests 9508, 9509 (Tel'athion the Impure's demented research, destroy the barrels, flask of purest water held back, Nobundo makes the water totem)
notes: Ownership: the chain starts and ends with Nobundo in the Exodar but plays out on Bloodmyst (Hidden Reef 3596, Foul Pool 3595, Tel'athion's Camp 3603); told here as a story, so Bloodmyst should not retell it or use 9500-9509/10490 but may write those places and Tel'athion as a KILL. The source of the pure water is contradictory in the DB (9504: naga ruins on this island; 9508, 9509: from Ashenvale), so it is left unnamed. Faction 1: 9500, 9501 and 10490 are draenei only; 9502 has no race limit but its giver Farseer Javad 23127 (Ironforge) is template 1638, hostile to the Horde; 10490's giver Farseer Umbrua 20407 (Stormwind) is template 1640. Fact-check: givers and enders verified (Sulaa, Javad, Umbrua to Nobundo; 9501 Nobundo to Aqueous; 9509 Aqueous back to Nobundo), so the chain is the Exodar's. Javad and Umbrua are not used by ironforge.json or stormwind.json.

title: The Draenei Call of Air
body: Air is the last of the four elements a draenei shaman comes to know, and Farseer Nobundo calls only those wise enough to go on. He sends them up the Wildwind Path on the northern face of the very mountain the Exodar crashed into. In a cave at its peak lives Velaada, one of his most accomplished pupils, who sees few visitors and heard of this one's coming on the wind. Air seems ethereal, she teaches, yet fills everything: her cave's rocks are mostly air, the oceans are saturated with it, and no fire burns without it, though the other elements had best not hear her say so. True wisdom waits with Susurrus, a lord of the winds, at the northern edge of the precipice. Unlike the other elements, he asks no task, judging that the shaman has done enough to atone for the ship that fell from his skies. He gives a portion of his own being and flies them back down to the city, where Nobundo, grinning at their ruffled hair, shapes it into an air totem.

title: Redemption
body: At Azure Watch, the paladin Tullas admits that even he at times struggles to follow the path of the Light, and he sends his best pupils to his own teacher, Jol, in the Vindicators' Sanctum, a room of the Vault of Lights wrapped in a vibrant glow. Jol's charge is to set paladins on the way to greater virtue. Her first lesson is a tome of divinity, to be read and understood. Then comes a test of compassion. Several young Stillpine shaman, allies of the draenei, stumbled on a Bristlelimb camp just past the bridge to Bloodmyst Isle and were slaughtered to the last. With a Symbol of Life the paladin raises one of them from death. The furbolg wakes bewildered, as anyone would who returns to the world of the living to find a strange being standing over them. All life is worth saving if it does not oppose us, Jol teaches; only enemies should be laid to rest for good. The power to call back the fallen is the paladin's from then on.
